title: Heuristically optimizing, synthesizing, and prioritizing measurement settings for quantum state tomography
summary: A key task in many quantum-computing applications, e.g., quantum simulation and quantum state tomography (QST), is to partition an arbitrary set of operators into mutually commuting subsets for efficient measurements. However, brute-force approaches to this task quickly become intractable as the number and dimensionality of operators grow. Here, we reformulate operator partitioning as a graph-coloring (GC) problem and develop an efficient computational framework to solve it, balancing accuracy and efficiency.
